series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

ndc_assessment.vintage: First (I)NDC round, as assessed by WRI CAIT (2016). Not the latest submission.
ndc_assessment.summary: "The Mitigation Contribution for Zimbabwe is given as 33% below the projected Business As Usual energy emissions per capita by 2030. This is a contribution target subject to the following conditions as a minimum: 1. "Full implementation by developed countries of their commitments relating to finance, technology and capacity pursuant to Article 4 of the Convention"; 2. Full, effective and sustained implementation of the Convention; 3. A post-2020 agreement addressing all elements set out in paragraph 5 of decision 1/CP.17 in a balanced and comprehensive manner; 4. Receiving contributions by developed countries on "all elements set out in paragraph 5 of decision 1/CP.17" relating to mitigation, adaptation, finance, technology development and transfer, and capacity-building in the context of a global and comprehensive agreement for the period beyond 2020." Zimbabwe also communicates an adaptation contribution, detailing the country's long-term and near-term adaptation visions, goals and targets. See the INDC for more information.
ndc_assessment.ghg_target: 33% reduction in energy emissions per capita by 2030 compared to the BAU scenario
ndc_assessment.$note: Third-party assessment of the first (I)NDC round. It is not merged into ndc.*, is not used by derive(), and does not appear on the dial as a target.

DS-05's rows are non-CO₂ gases only and are not comparable with the others; that is also why DS-05 is absent from series.observed, where a shorter curve would read as a disagreement rather than a difference of scope. by_source carries each source whole.

verdict.text: The registry's current submission for this Party is NDC3.0 Country Statement, filed 2025-02-10. 49 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (3). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-02 35.8 MtCO₂e, DS-35 31.1 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against. It submitted BTR1. 5 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 35.4 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: 33% reduction in energy emissions per capita by 2030 compared to the BAU scenario It was classed conditional. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.33°C under SSP1-2.6 to +4.74°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
